moved forward while waving thank you at the driver in the black truck he heard a loud slap on his hood. du #1 stated he stopped immediately and saw ped1 in front of his car with both hands on the records.public_safe_text: du #1 stated he was leaving the parking lot at the listed location which is a well med facility. du #1 stated he was facing west leaving his parking slot when he stopped in front of the well med doctors facility for a black truck. du #1 stated he stopped in his aisle for this black truck whom had the right of way driving in front of the well med facility which was perpendicular to his aisle. du #1 stated the driver in the black truck wanted the parking slot he just vacated so he waved du #1 to continue his left turn in front of his truck. du #1 stated as he moved forward while waving thank you at the driver in the black truck he heard a loud slap on his hood. du #1 stated he stopped immediately and saw ped1 in front of his car with both hands on the center of his hood. du #1 stated when he stopped the momentum of his car moving forward coupled with ped1 locked arms and hands on his hood forced ped1 to take several steps backwards. du #1 stated he didn't hit ped1. du #1 stated after he stopped his forward motion he saw ped1 take several steps backwards before tripping over a curb and falling to the sidewalk in front of the well med facility. du #1 then said he noticed ped1 was on his cell phone while walking towards the well med facility just before he moved forward. du #1 stated he immediately exited his car after stopping to check on ped1 who told him he wasn't hurt. du #1 stated then w1, whom is a doctor at the well med facility, came out and checked ped1. du #1 stated w1 told him ped1 was not hurt, but just as a precaution he would take him into his office and examine him since he is a patient under his care. du #1 stated w1 told him ped1 didn't want to be examined or transported by ems so w1 had his nurse call 911 to cancel ems. du #1 stated w1 told him ped1 was not hurt and he would take care of him so there was no need for du #1 to remain at the scene. du #1 stated he gave w1 his business card just in [case id] needed to contact him. when we arrived ped1 was in a room at the well med facility and he told us his hip was hurting him a little bit after landing on the curb. i then contacted w1 who told me he didn't see the accident and his preliminary examination showed that ped1 was not hurt. w1 then gave me du #1 business card so i called him to see where he had gone. du #1 told me he had just ordered food at a local restaurant, tink a tako, at the corner of van cleave/wurzbach. i drove over to meet with du #1. du #1 explained the accident to me exactly as descibed above. i told du #1 if he should ever be in an accident in the future he should wait for police to arrive before leaving. i checked du #1 car and there was no damage to the front end. we did however notice two hand prints on the center of the hood. i then contacted sup sgt. christopher johnson #3261 and told him how this accident occurred. sup sgt nicholas johnson #3261 told me this wasn't a hit/run accident which was my thinking as well. i did mention to sup sgt nicholas johnson #3261 that i would contact traffic investigations as a precaution and he agreed. i then contacted tid det. lori herries #2488 who told me to write this call as an accident and not a hit/run. tid det. lori herries #2488 also told me i didn't need to get a uedi to take photos of the ped1 hand prints on du #1 car. coban/bwc on.

records.deidentified_narrative: accident occurred in private property parking lot of peter piper pizza involving us postal service (usps) mail delivery truck. unit 2 ped stated she was walking out of the ace cash next to the peter piper pizza and when crossing in the parking lot she observed unit 1. ped stated she saw the driver of unit 1 looking to the side either at the mail of a cell phone and accelerated hitting ped on her right shoulder with the front of the vehicle. ped stated after getting hit by unit 1 driver asked if she was ok and ped replied her right arm was sore and hurting. ped stated driver told her he had to leave due to needing to make his rounds and deliver the mail. ped walked to her vehicle and when she looked back unit 1 had left scene in unknown direction. ped relocated home to make report of hit and run involving usps vehicle.***wh #2386 (tid): i was assigned as the lead investigator in this case. i conducted a follow-up investigation into the reported incident. i conducted recorded interviews with ped and unit #1 driver. i also located surveillance video that captured the incident. following this investigation, i determined that the crash likely did not occur and the events of the incident did not occur as described by ped. during my investigation, i located video surveillance from [roadway] which showed the ped walk in front of unit #1, a mail delivery truck (grumman llv) owned by the united states postal service. the video surveillance shows unit #1 stop abruptly. the surveillance video did not show if an impact on ped by unit #1 occurred, due to the angle of the camera view. the video surveillance shows that the ped did not stumble into a pole or drop a package that she was carrying, which ped claimed occurred. the surveillance video showed the ped speak with the driver of unit #1 and hand packages to the driver of unit #1. the surveillance video shows ped walk back [roadway] away prior to unit #1 leaving the scene. unit #1 driver stated that he was not sure if unit #1 impacted ped but is assuming that it did based on the statement made by ped that her arm was hurting. unit #1 driver offered to call emergency medical services for her and notified his supervisor of the incident, which was confirmed on his phone call history and verified by his supervisor. this investigation is being closed as unfounded. it is unable to be proven that a crash occurred or that a crime occurred.***
